leftEvidence.title: David gives Solomon plans before the assembly

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David gathers leaders, recounts his desire and God’s choice, charges Israel and Solomon, gives plans and weights, and tells Solomon to be strong because God and organized workers are with him.
points.right: David names Solomon’s youth and the palace’s scale, gives his own treasure, asks who will offer willingly, and leaders respond until the people rejoice.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places private succession becomes a public handoff of design, responsibility, and personnel inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the prepared project becomes shared material participation inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Chronicles 28:1–21 and 1 Chronicles 29:1–9 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Succession, Retelling, and Temple Preparation” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: David and the assembly give for the house

payload.tension: 1 Chronicles 28:1–21 foregrounds private succession becomes a public handoff of design, responsibility, and personnel; 1 Chronicles 29:1–9 foregrounds the prepared project becomes shared material participation. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
